vo: Drop a coin down a hole through the Earth. It never lands. So why does it keep coming back?
cap: Drop a coin through the Earth.

vo: Not because it hits the bottom. At the centre, gravity is zero, yet the coin is moving at nearly eight kilometres every second.
Think of a swing. At the lowest point nothing pulls it, but it still swings right past, because speed carries it.
It takes about forty two minutes to reach the other side. There it stops for one instant, then drops back.
Eighty four minutes, again and again, forever. Send this to someone who thinks falling has a bottom. Because a coin never lands. It just keeps dropping, a coin down a hole through the Earth.
